92	## 1. Reliability Diagram（校准图）

94	**用途**：显示模型 confidence bin vs accuracy，对角线 = 完美校准。
95	
96	```python
97	def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
98	                              label='', color='#0072B2',
99	                              title='Reliability Diagram',
100	                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
101	    """
102	    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
103	    """
104	    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
105	    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []
106	
107	    for i in range(n_bins):
108	        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
109	        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
110	        if mask.sum() > 0:
111	            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
112	            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
113	            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
114	        else:
115	            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
116	            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
117	            bin_counts.append(0)
118	
119	    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
120	    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)
121	
122	    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
123	        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
124	        sharex=True
125	    )
126	
127	    # 主图：gaps
128	    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
129	                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
130	    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
131	                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
132	    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
133	    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
134	    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
135	    ax_main.set_title(title)
136	    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
137	    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)
138	
139	    # ECE annotation
140	    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
141	                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
142	    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
143	                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
144	                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))
145	
146	    # 直方图（样本密度）
147	    ax_hist.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_counts, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
148	                color=color, alpha=0.5)
149	    ax_hist.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
150	    ax_hist.set_xlabel('Confidence')
151	
152	    plt.tight_layout()
153	    plt.savefig(outpath)
154	    plt.close()
155	    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
156	```

182	def plot_ece_heatmap(delta_ece_matrix, methods, datasets,
183	                     title='ΔECE Heatmap (vs FP16)',
184	                     outpath='ece_heatmap.pdf'):
185	    """
186	    delta_ece_matrix: shape (n_methods, n_datasets), 正=ECE 恶化, 负=改善
187	    """
188	    import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
189

191	
192	    # 发散色图（中心=0, 红=恶化, 蓝=改善）
193	    vmax = np.nanmax(np.abs(delta_ece_matrix))
194	    norm = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-vmax, vcenter=0, vmax=vmax)
195	    cmap = plt.cm.RdBu_r
196	
197	    im = ax.imshow(delta_ece_matrix, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, aspect='auto')
198	
199	    # 数值标注
200	    for i in range(len(methods)):
201	        for j in range(len(datasets)):
202	            val = delta_ece_matrix[i, j]
203	            if not np.isnan(val):
204	                color = 'white' if abs(val) > vmax * 0.6 else 'black'
205	                sign = '+' if val > 0 else ''
206	                ax.text(j, i, f'{sign}{val:.1%}', ha='center', va='center',
207	                        fontsize=9, color=color, fontweight='bold')
208

```python
def plot_reliability_diagram(confidences, accuracies, n_bins=10,
                              label='', color='#0072B2',
                              title='Reliability Diagram',
                              outpath='reliability.pdf'):
    """
    confidences, accuracies: 各样本的 confidence 和 binary correct (0/1)
    """
    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
    bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts = [], [], []

    for i in range(n_bins):
        lo, hi = bin_edges[i], bin_edges[i+1]
        mask = (confidences >= lo) & (confidences < hi)
        if mask.sum() > 0:
            bin_accs.append(accuracies[mask].mean())
            bin_confs.append(confidences[mask].mean())
            bin_counts.append(mask.sum())
        else:
            bin_accs.append(float('nan'))
            bin_confs.append((lo + hi) / 2)
            bin_counts.append(0)

    bin_accs = np.array(bin_accs)
    bin_confs = np.array(bin_confs)

    fig, (ax_main, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
        2, 1, figsize=(4, 4.5), gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [3, 1]},
        sharex=True
    )

    # 主图：gaps
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.7, label='Accuracy', zorder=2)
    ax_main.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_confs - bin_accs, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                bottom=bin_accs, color='red', alpha=0.3, label='Gap', zorder=2)
    ax_main.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=1, zorder=3, label='Perfect')
    ax_main.set_xlim(0, 1); ax_main.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax_main.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
    ax_main.set_title(title)
    ax_main.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
    ax_main.grid(True, alpha=0.3, zorder=1)

    # ECE annotation
    ece = np.nansum(np.array(bin_counts) / sum(bin_counts) *
                    np.abs(bin_accs - bin_confs))
    ax_main.text(0.98, 0.02, f'ECE={ece:.3f}', transform=ax_main.transAxes,
                 ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9,
                 bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

    # 直方图（样本密度）
    ax_hist.bar(bin_edges[:-1], bin_counts, width=1/n_bins, align='edge',
                color=color, alpha=0.5)
    ax_hist.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=9)
    ax_hist.set_xlabel('Confidence')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')
```

def plot_ece_heatmap(delta_ece_matrix, methods, datasets,
                     title='ΔECE Heatmap (vs FP16)',
                     outpath='ece_heatmap.pdf'):
    """
    delta_ece_matrix: shape (n_methods, n_datasets), 正=ECE 恶化, 负=改善
    """
    import matplotlib.colors as mcolors

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(len(datasets) * 1.2, len(methods) * 0.8 + 1))

    # 发散色图（中心=0, 红=恶化, 蓝=改善）
    vmax = np.nanmax(np.abs(delta_ece_matrix))
    norm = mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-vmax, vcenter=0, vmax=vmax)
    cmap = plt.cm.RdBu_r

    im = ax.imshow(delta_ece_matrix, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, aspect='auto')

    # 数值标注
    for i in range(len(methods)):
        for j in range(len(datasets)):
            val = delta_ece_matrix[i, j]
            if not np.isnan(val):
                color = 'white' if abs(val) > vmax * 0.6 else 'black'
                sign = '+' if val > 0 else ''
                ax.text(j, i, f'{sign}{val:.1%}', ha='center', va='center',
                        fontsize=9, color=color, fontweight='bold')

    ax.set_xticks(range(len(datasets)))
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(methods)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(datasets, rotation=30, ha='right')
    ax.set_yticklabels(methods)
    ax.set_title(title)

    cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    cbar.set_label('ΔECE (quantized − FP16)')
    cbar.ax.axhline(0, color='k', linewidth=0.8)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath)
    plt.close()
    print(f'Saved: {outpath}')

def wilson_ci(p, n, z=1.96):
    if n == 0: return 0, 0
    denom = 1 + z**2 / n
    center = (p + z**2 / (2*n)) / denom
    half = z * np.sqrt((p*(1-p) + z**2/(4*n)) / n) / denom
    return max(0, center - half), min(1, center + half)

\begin{abstract}
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models report high Collision Avoidance Rates (CAR) on safety benchmarks, yet we show these metrics are contaminated by action collapse.
On SafeLIBERO, an SDF-augmented Pi0 achieves 91.5\% CAR while 99.6\% of its safe episodes exhibit end-effector displacement below 0.1\,mm---the robot is frozen, not safe.

Our analysis further reveals that end-effector-only Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision is neither necessary nor structurally sufficient for collision avoidance.
It is counterproductive at inference time: three ground-truth oracle variants all reduce dfCAR below unrefined baselines, as SDF gradients repelling the end-effector drive arm links into obstacles.
Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ (56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a marginal signal (58.25\%$\,\pm\,$0.35, $p{\approx}0.039$) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the demonstration distribution, requiring further investigation.
Per-task avoidance patterns remain identical across all conditions, indicating that collision avoidance arises from collision-free demonstration data rather than geometric supervision.

\begin{abstract}
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models report high Collision Avoidance Rates (CAR) on safety benchmarks, yet we show these metrics are contaminated by action collapse.
On SafeLIBERO, an SDF-augmented Pi0 achieves 91.5\% CAR while 99.6\% of its safe episodes exhibit end-effector displacement below 0.1\,mm---the robot is frozen, not safe.
We present displacement-filtered CAR (dfCAR), which excludes sub-threshold episodes, as a corrective metric; the bimodal displacement distribution makes it robust across a $[2, 200]$\,mm threshold range.
Our analysis further reveals that end-effector-only Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision is neither necessary nor structurally sufficient for collision avoidance.
It is counterproductive at inference time: three ground-truth oracle variants all reduce dfCAR below unrefined baselines, as SDF gradients repelling the end-effector drive arm links into obstacles.
Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ (56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a marginal signal (58.25\%$\,\pm\,$0.35, $p{\approx}0.039$) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the demonstration distribution, requiring further investigation.
Per-task avoidance patterns remain identical across all conditions, indicating that collision avoidance arises from collision-free demonstration data rather than geometric supervision.
Displacement filtering is necessary for meaningful VLA safety evaluation; EE-only geometric supervision can be neither credited with nor expected to deliver collision avoidance.
\end{abstract}

\begin{abstract}
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models report high Collision Avoidance Rates (CAR) on safety benchmarks, yet we show these metrics are contaminated by action collapse.
On SafeLIBERO, an SDF-augmented Pi0 achieves 91.5\% CAR while 99.6\% of its safe episodes exhibit end-effector displacement below 0.1\,mm---the robot is frozen, not safe.
We present displacement-filtered CAR (dfCAR), which excludes sub-threshold episodes, as a corrective metric; the bimodal displacement distribution makes it robust across a $[2, 200]$\,mm threshold range.
Our analysis further reveals that end-effector-only Signed Distance Field (SDF) supervision is neither necessary nor structurally sufficient for collision avoidance.
It is counterproductive at inference time: three ground-truth oracle variants all reduce dfCAR below unrefined baselines, as SDF gradients repelling the end-effector drive arm links into obstacles.
Its contribution during training is dose-dependent: LoRA-only fine-tuning raises dfCAR from 26.8\% to 54.83\%$\,\pm\,$2.25, matching SDF-augmented training at $\lambda{=}0.005$ (54.5\%$\,\pm\,$2.29) and $\lambda{=}0.01$ (56.33\%$\,\pm\,$1.61); at $\lambda{=}0.1$, two of three seeds show a marginal signal (58.25\%$\,\pm\,$0.35, $p{\approx}0.039$) whose per-task avoidance pattern still mirrors the demonstration distribution, requiring further investigation.
Per-task avoidance patterns remain identical across all conditions, indicating that collision avoidance arises from collision-free demonstration data rather than geometric supervision.
Displacement filtering is necessary for meaningful VLA safety evaluation; EE-only geometric supervision can be neither credited with nor expected to deliver collision avoidance.
